title: St Vincent's launches AI Clinical Council
source_used: Cyber Daily (own report, citing a St Vincent's statement); CathNews also read
key_facts: St Vincent's, which operates 25 aged-care facilities and 12 private and public hospitals in Australia, convened the first meetings of its AI Clinical Council on 8 and 9 October 2026 (Cyber Daily); CathNews of 9 Oct says the two-day meeting was in Melbourne.

The council aims to explore the ethical and effective use of AI across all St Vincent's services and to advise on how to identify, evaluate and scale AI technologies that improve patient care and clinician wellbeing (CathNews).

St Vincent's said the council will not replace existing clinical, governance or approval processes, but will help ensure AI decisions are informed by frontline clinical expertise, operational realities and the voices of patients and residents.
Chief medical officer Dr Chris Robinson said the guiding principle is 'Human care first; AI where it helps' (CathNews).
St Vincent's has also written to the Prime Minister encouraging the inclusion of healthcare providers in devising Australian Standards for AI use (Cyber Daily).
Cyber Daily says the meetings were held under the direction of Jonathan Ruane, a senior lecturer at the MIT Sloan School of Management; CathNews does not mention him.
No specific AI tool, rule or patient result was announced.
quote_evidence: The council aims to explore the “ethical and effective” use of AI across all of St Vincent’s services.
The council will not replace existing clinical, governance or approval processes.
In addition, St Vincent’s has addressed a letter to the Prime Minister encouraging the inclusion of healthcare providers in devising Australian Standards for AI use.
why_it_matters_hint: A large health and aged-care provider has created a clinical body to guide its AI use, but this is a governance step with no tool, rule or result announced yet.
event_date: Council met 8-9 Oct 2026 (CathNews 9 Oct, Tech Business News 8 Oct per Google News listing); Pulse+IT and Cyber Daily covered it on 12 Oct 2026
